title: Why the minimum payment keeps you broke for 19 years

scenes.text: Your credit card bill says: minimum payment, $150. Pay just that, and this $5,000 takes almost 20 years to pay off.
Mike and Jake both owe $5,000 at 24% interest. Mike pays the minimum. Jake pays $250 a month.
Two years later, Jake is completely debt-free. Mike still owes $3,850.
Mike keeps paying. And paying. He finally finishes after nineteen and a half years.
Total interest? Mike paid $8,887. Jake paid $1,449.
Jake's extra $100 a month saved him $7,438 and 17 years of payments.
So never pay just the minimum. Pick a fixed amount, and keep paying it, even when the minimum drops.
What's your credit card's interest rate? Drop it in the comments.

props.disclaimer: Example: $5,000 at 24% APR, minimum = interest + 1% of balance. Your card's terms may differ. Not financial advice.
